title: SMART Guidelines KG L1 classes
description: The classes a L1 knowledge-graph node can be. smart-base document kinds and extractions name them as `sgkg-l1#<code>`. GENERATED by smart-base/L1/schemas/emit.ts from smart-base/L1/schemas/l1.ts: do not hand-edit; change the layer source and run `npm run build` in smart-base/L1/schemas/.

source.note: smart-base/L1/schemas/l1.ts, the layer's `classes`: id, name, note and iri. Classes the layer no longer has stay, retired.

codes.label: Publication
codes.definition: A WHO publication: a guideline of any of the handbook's types, a position paper, a summary table, a classification, implementation guidance, or a supplement. Metadata follows Dublin Core.

codes.label: Publication section
codes.definition: A chapter, annex or numbered section, at any depth.

codes.label: Publication element
codes.definition: One printed block: a table, a table row, a footnote, a figure, a chart, an image, a flowchart, a box or a list. It records where something is printed and exactly what is printed that no content node holds. It carries no meaning of its own; meaning lives in content nodes, joined by presentedIn.

codes.label: Recommendation
codes.definition: A normative statement from a WHO guideline. Kinds other than a graded recommendation (context-specific, research-only, good practice statement, no-recommendation) are the same node with a different kind.

codes.label: Remark
codes.definition: A remark attached to a recommendation (handbook §10.6). May also be printed as a table footnote.

codes.label: Key question
codes.definition: A question in PICO format, framed before the evidence search (handbook §7.1–7.4). P and C are verbatim text with codes through crossReferences; I is also joined to a catalogued intervention; O is the outcome node.

codes.label: Outcome
codes.definition: An outcome a guideline group chose to judge a key question by, with its importance in this guideline (handbook §7.6). A node because evidence attaches to it and one list is shared by several questions (ANC Web annex 1). Flat: one node per specific outcome.

codes.label: Evidence
codes.definition: One row of an evidence profile: the evidence for one outcome of one key question, with its certainty (handbook §9.2).

codes.label: Health intervention
codes.definition: An intervention identified in a WHO catalogue or classification (UHC Compendium, ICHI, CDHI), digital interventions included. A peer of recommendation, not a recommendation. A DAK may draw on both.

codes.label: Indicator
codes.definition: A WHO indicator, identified by its published reference number. Printed in several places (HIV SI 2022: summary list, Table 2.3, reference sheet) and stored once.

codes.label: Citation
codes.definition: One citation string exactly as written in a DAK artefact. A cell holding several citations yields several nodes. Content-addressed in the DAK's namespace, so one string is one node across artefacts.

codes.label: Reference entry
codes.definition: One row of a DAK artefact's own reference list: '(1)' and the full bibliographic text and URL it stands for. Resolved once; every citation numbered to it shares the result.

codes.label: Terminology code
codes.definition: A code in an external terminology — ICD-10, ICD-11, SNOMED CT, ATC, or a WHO classification such as CDHI. CROSS-REFERENCE ONLY. It records system, code and display, and asserts NOTHING about the terminology: no hierarchy, no subsumption, no synonyms, no post-coordination. The terminology has its own authority, its own release cycle and its own tooling, and a partial copy here would be wrong within one release. Resolve meaning against the terminology server, not against this graph.

codes.label: Population
codes.definition: Retired in L1 3.0: the P of a PICO question is verbatim text on its key-question, coded through crossReferences.

codes.label: Intervention
codes.definition: Retired in L1 3.0: the I of a PICO question is on its key-question, joined to a catalogued health-intervention.

codes.label: Comparator
codes.definition: Retired in L1 3.0: the C of a PICO question is verbatim text on its key-question, coded through crossReferences.

codes.label: Schedule
codes.definition: Retired in L1 3.0: timing is a slot on the recommendation; L2's scheduling-logic implements the recommendation.

codes.label: Schedule entry
codes.definition: Retired in L1 3.0: timing is a slot on the recommendation; L2's scheduling-logic implements the recommendation.

codes.label: External artefact
codes.definition: Moved to L2 in 3.0 unchanged: a DAK file is the DAK's material, not WHO content. Use sgkg-l2#external-artifact.
